AWPTCM-T33275.objective:
• Enhanced recovery mode can be enabled and disabled per EPSR domain via CLI.
  • When enhanced recovery is enabled on a transit node, a Link Forward Request is transmitted on the control VLAN when a port comes up.
  • When a Permission Link Forward is received in response to a Link Forward Request, the port transitions to the forwarding state.
  • The EPSR master transmits a Permission Link Forward in response to a Link Forward Request when no health checks are circulating.
  • Enhanced recovery behavior is independent per domain: disabling the mode on the master or on a transit affects recovery only for domains where it is disabled.
  • Single link failure and recovery with enhanced recovery enabled completes successfully with no loop forming at any time.
  • Multiple and partial link failures/recoveries with enhanced recovery allow traffic to flow in recovered segments while the ring returns to the complete state.
  • Enhanced recovery uses the Link Forward Request / Permission Link Forward protocol to optimize recovery compared to standard EPSR behavior.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability. Primary coverage from TestLink Enhanced Recovery family (AWP-145, AWP-4076, AWP-4077, AWP-4078, AWP-4083, AWP-4084, AWP-4086 and related multi-domain cases). ART coverage from 1334.3001.6-10 (Link Forward Request / Permission Link Forward protocol on master and transit) + 1340 (CR41421 timing).
Configure an EPSR domain and enable enhanced recovery (`epsr <ep> enhancedrecovery enable`). Confirm the configuration is accepted and show epsr reports the mode as enabled for the domain.

With enhanced recovery enabled on a transit node, induce a port down/up (or link failure/recovery). Verify that a Link Forward Request is sent on the control VLAN and that a Permission Link Forward response causes the port to transition to forwarding.

Perform the equivalent port/link recovery on the master node with enhanced recovery enabled. Confirm the master transmits Permission Link Forward as expected and the ring returns to Complete state with no loop.

Configure multiple EPSR domains. Enable enhanced recovery on some domains only. Induce failures and verify that recovery (forwarding / traffic flow) occurs only on the domains where enhanced recovery is enabled.
Test single link failure + recovery with enhanced recovery enabled. Confirm no loop forms at any time and the ring returns to Complete state.
Test multiple link failures (two or more) followed by partial then full recovery. Confirm recovered segments allow traffic flow and the full ring eventually reaches Complete state with no loops.
Verify that disabling enhanced recovery on the master or a transit changes recovery behavior for that domain (e.g. segments do not forward until full ring recovery).
